webster.text: Heat or warmth; as the fervor of a summer's day.

more.text: Heat of mind; ardor; warm or animated zeal and earnestness in the duties of religion, particularly in prayer.

example.quote: The Constitution had then wisely made him, as a man, responsible by the influence of fame, his character, and his feelings ; as a citizen, they have postponed the period at which he could be tried with propriety until the fervor of party and cool reflection can determine his fate.
example.cite: Jonathan Elliot, ed., The Debates in the Several State Conventions on the Adoption of the Federal Constitution, vol. 4, South Carolina House of Representatives (debate on calling the convention), Hon. ROBERT BARNWELL, January 17, 1788 (2d ed. 1836)
